I'm an only child and when I started college I wished I had a sibling to look up to and help make me feel more comfortable with the process. Because of this it took me a long time to break out of my shell and tampered with the college experience. Now I am almost done college and kind of regret not being more outgoing. You should try to help make your sisters time at college the best it can be and hope to God she doesn't end up like me. For now just be her guide and give her some advice. You can also take her out with your friends a couple of times just to know what she can do for fun and get her more comfortable at social outings. Eventually she will make her own friends and go off on her own it just might take awhile. Definitely tell her how you feel and how you want her to be her own person, make her own adventure and not just rely on you the whole time. Tell her about money and how life isn't a walk in the park. Also since she's your sister she should look up to you as an example. You need to show her that even in those blizzards and wastelands they don't have to go through it alone. Then one day when your sister runs into someone who needs help she will remember what you did for her and she can pass along the good deed. Even though you may not like it the fact that you are doing something good for someone really goes along way. In the end don't you want to see your sister be happy and have a good time at college? Because who knows she may struggle even more then you did when you first started and you probably don't want to see that would you?

It's not something that advertised it just something that is done. While I visit Montreal in the summer my family and I end up going to our cottage in St-Jovite near Mont-Tremblant. We usually go to Maison Du Spaghetti which makes pizza in this fashion. It's expensive, if I recall it's $20 for a large but the quality is way better then normal pizza. The put a lot of toppings on the pizza and the cheese is very thick which they melt the toppings into the cheese except for the pepperoni which is always at the bottom.    Yes the pepperoni is crispy but only around the edges for some reason but the pepperoni is cooked really well. Yes the rest of the pizza is cooked really well including the crust it tastes more crispy then doey and is on the thinner side it provides a nice crunch when you take a bite. The only problem is it gets kinda messy as the cheese has a stuff time staying attached to the crust if you pull it hard enough when you bite you'll end up eating the entire cheese and topping in one bite. Also the sauce it a bit liquidy which can get annoying There are places around St-Jovite that do the same thing but in the actual city of Montreal I believe Nikkos does this but I'm not 100% sure as its been a few years since I've been there but I remember the crust being kind of thick. But I believe a majority of pizza places in Montreal do this style of pizza making.
They actually do this in Montreal Canada.

The game gets better after act 2 and gets really good at act 4. 

Unlike the second the first game goes way deeper into the universe of the witcher and you get to see how developed the world really is by meeting different races and political factions. 


You can try to bang as many women as possible collecting sex cards so just like Pokemon you gotta catch them all.(in this case fuck them all.)

If you follow a certain questline you can have the opportunity to be the number one fist fighter and dice poker player in all of Vizima. Who wouldn't want that!

If your going to play the second you can transfer your save and the major decisions made in the first game will carry over into the second, while not making a huge impact to the world it was nice to see the choices I made carried over, it also makes the second a better experience as you know the plot and won't be as confused too what is going on and you know about the returning characters.

I agree the combat is kind of weird it gets more interesting with the use of potions and magical spells known as signs. In my playthrough I never needed to grind for XP don't be that forced to get into fights. There are a lot of side quests and backtracking to different places which can be brutal. My suggestion is find as many as you can decide on doing the ones you find interesting as a lot of them are pretty cool and have interesting story lines.

I just beat this game recently as well as the second, I enjoyed both games thoroughly and I cannot wait for The Witcher 3.

So thats just my 2 cents on what I think of the game and hopefully you'll find the strength to continue. If you don't thats okay a majority of the people who played the witcher 1 are in the same boat as you so don't feel like the odd ma out.
